title: Absolute-constant square-root delocalization of binary Hayes conductor layers
statement: Let ell >= 200, let n be 2 ell + 1 or 2 ell + 2, put D_e=N_n(e)-2^(n-ell), and let D_[j]=P_j D-P_(j-1)D be its exact-conductor martingale layer. For every 4<=j<=ell and every class e, |D_[j](e)|^2 is at most 4 (j-1)^2 2^(j-1+n-2ell). THIS PROPOSITION IS FALSE: the exact fixed-conductor recurrence gives a level-j=4 violation at the even endpoint (ell,n)=(343,688), beyond the degree-400 finite handoff.

evidence.supports: The exact level-four degree recurrence gives a normalized squared constant strictly greater than four at degree 688, the even endpoint for ell=343.
evidence.notes: The level-j sibling difference is independent of the ambient ell once ell>=j. The arbitrary-precision recurrence is seeded by exact population transforms and its first propagated row is independently checked. It avoids allocating E_343 while retaining the exact E_4 endpoint layer.

provenance.source: native exact level-four Hayes population and conductor-layer normalization

notes: This refutes the concrete absolute-constant target selected from rows through ell=20. More generally, simultaneous recurrence of the finitely many normalized Frobenius eigenvalues at a fixed level j shows that the supremum over endpoint degrees of the normalized kappa_j is exactly the trivial ceiling 2^((j-1)/2), so no absolute K can work uniformly in j. It does not refute a polynomial-in-ell loss, because the recurrent degrees can grow rapidly with j. The replacement conjectured fact uses squared loss 4 ell^4 and the existing endpoint implication.
